channel.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check
channel.description: A weekday rundown of west-central Miami-Dade (Westchester, Sweetwater, Kendall, Doral) and County Hall, with balanced coverage across outlets.
channel.itunes:author: Hark

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Wednesday, October 28
item.description: Sheriff ends commissioner security program as mayor pushes back; Doral gala draws criticism; record king tide; Miami e-bike rules; ballot counter. Music: "Pamgaea" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Tuesday, October 27
item.description: The sheriff pulls security details from the mayor and commissioners as the county budget fight escalates, Amendment 3 job-loss projections land, and a west Miami-Dade data center gets a name. Plus business, public safety, king tides and the ballot counter. Music: "Life of Riley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Monday, October 26
item.description: Sheriff Cordero-Stutz ends the county's sergeant at arms escorts on Nov. 9 as her budget fight with Mayor Levine Cava escalates; the mayor holds off on Brightline's Coastal Link; and M-DCPS loses nearly 16,000 students as the school tax shares the ballot with Amendment 3. Plus Sweetwater bodycam video, the weekend king tides and the early-voting count. Music: "Pamgaea" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Friday, October 23
item.description: Friday's edition, in public radio style: the sheriff ends the security program for the mayor and commissioners as the budget fight grows, Miami-to-Aventura commuter train funding returns, and a lawsuit seeks a vote on the Seaquarium marina. Miami-Dade schools lose nearly 16,000 students, plus the ballot counter. Music: "Pamgaea" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Thursday, October 22
item.description: A lawsuit seeks a countywide vote on the Seaquarium marina, the sheriff defends her cowboy hats, and Gov. DeSantis pitches Amendment 3 at the Doral sheriff's office. Also: Hialeah's paid texts for the mayor, a new teachers' contract tied to the Nov. 3 school tax, and a king-tide flood watch. Music: "Life of Riley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Wednesday, October 21
item.description: Commissioners advance the Seaquarium plan and approve a Miami Vice film incentive; Metro fares rise to $2.75 in January; the Sheriff's $132,500 cowboy hats draw fire; and teachers' raises hinge on the Nov. 3 school referendum. Music: "Local Forecast" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Tuesday, October 20
item.description: The County Commission votes today on a rent-free 99-year lease for 800 apartments at 9250 West Flagler and on how far to promote Grand Theft Auto VI; the mayor vetoes a freeze on the Doral incinerator demolition; North Miami's mayor is knocked off the ballot; and Archbishop Wenski calls the state's Catholic school voucher threat bullying. Today's edition is written in the style of a public radio newscast. Music: "Pamgaea" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Monday, October 19
item.description: Early voting opens in Miami-Dade, a Miami judge signs a state arrest warrant for Raúl Castro, and the County Commission takes up an 800-apartment land lease beside the West Dade Government Center on Tuesday. Also: the school tax and seven county referendums, and the weekend in the county. Music: "Life of Riley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), licensed under CC BY 4.0, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Friday, October 16
item.description: Doral's mayor addresses immigration fear in her State of the City, and next week's county votes take shape: 800 workforce apartments by the West Dade Government Center, the Seaquarium land use and the Arsht billboards. Vouchers now outspend public schools in Miami-Dade, and weekend rain is on the way.

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Thursday, October 15
item.description: Ballot-and-budget morning: Save Gramps rallies voters, the School Board approves Success Academy co-location with possible layoffs, and the Columbus High-Banyan Elementary arc. Plus Amendment 3 vs. the schools tax, a Medley shooting, and a weekend flood threat.

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Wednesday, October 14
item.description: Transit cuts and a possible county transit authority, the Doral incinerator-fee spat, the collapsed airport hotel, and the Nov. 3 ballot: schools referendum and Amendment 3. Coverage of west-central neighborhoods was thin today.

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Tuesday, October 13
item.description: Commissioners bristle at the GTA 6 Vice City ad deal, campaign money and marina-lease stories heat up before Nov. 3, and the school tax referendum could decide teacher supplements. Plus a cockfighting bust, Knaus Berry Farm's opening day, and state news touching Dade.

item.title: Miami-Dade Vibe Check: Monday, October 12
item.description: A pocketbook Monday: the county raises bus and Metrorail fares 50 cents while Metromover stays free, the Sheriff disputes a record budget, and Angie Nixon campaigns in Sweetwater. Plus disabled-parking permit cancellations, school vouchers, the weekend after Hurricane Isaias, and what Amendment 3 would cost the county.

item.title: Welcome to Miami-Dade Vibe Check
item.description: A short test episode. Weekday episodes start Monday at 8 am.
